svg.text: Emilia | revised guides for review
V2: softer front transition, longer side return, continuous oblique wrap. No mesh edits.
Magenta = hypothesis. Amber = unresolved shape. Gray = unchanged context; no physical scale.
FRONT
Continuous upper-to-lower transition
Standing front supports
cloth placement, not hidden
body width or medial depth.
upper transition
broad turn
gradual return
Lower join: meet the existing ribcage smoothly.
Replaced the near-vertical box sides with
a gradual outward transition and long taper.
No shelf, band, medial flattening or front island.
Fullness is unresolved by the front view alone.
One surface wrapping around the ribcage
Oblique views test wrapping.
Hands / tilt block the join;
do not transfer the outline.
near turn
far return
Lower join: meet the existing ribcage smoothly.
Preserved the continuous ribcage-wrap idea.
The lower near-side arc returns gradually.
Thin interior lines indicate flow, not a groove.
No separate anterior objects or cups are implied.
SIDE
Projection dissolves into a long return
No true side in this frame.
Lean + arms hide the join;
depth remains hypothetical.
soft onset
fullest region
long gradual return
Lower join: meet the existing ribcage smoothly.
The return is one extended arc, not a short
inward bend followed by an upright reset.
No ribcage notch or new abdomen target.
Neither running nor leaning sets literal depth.
These are revised hypotheses, not approved modeling targets.
The standing and original front frames constrain garment/body separation; the oblique frames test continuity.
The running and leaning frames supply support only. They are not neutral side blueprints.
No previous Claude / Devin render, failed mesh, or clothed edge was used as an anatomical target.
All model files stay locked. Body, garment and every surrounding part remain paused until guide approval.
